description: Real-agent eval (amendment bb664f58910f section 2 / bb664f58910f (2), tier real_agent): one headless Claude Code session per item at k=1 (evals.runner.ClaudeCodeAgent; the operator's Claude Code login, no paid API) behind the runner's tool gate: read-only tools only, so no case-store writer, no plx.act or other action or MC write (a call outside the set is refused, never forwarded, and counted), no built-in tools, no other MCP server, no credential in the session environment. Parts, in budget order: live_bc (the headline): at least 20 Business-Central-rooted oracle items sampled by the independent oracle from its own GET-only BC (and, when configured, mail and SharePoint) reads, answered through the persistent host's own MCP server (operating.host mcp over PLX_WORKBENCH_STATE_DIR: the BC, mail and SharePoint captures and their projection, no Portal read) as the named reader in PLX_EVAL_READER, each session with a fresh single-use agent ticket signed with PLX_WORKBENCH_SESSION_SECRET; without that identity the part reads as the declared eval principal (operating.eval_principal, examples/eval_principal.json: staff:operations and staff:sales, no marking, no action path), labelled reader eval_principal in the result; the A6 permission proof (denied_leaks) is never made by it and still requires PLX_EVAL_READER (access.a6_permission_proof says so; never a fixture principal; ticket source: docs/decisions/2026-10-07-live-agent-metric-reader-ticket.md), and oracle strata the Portal outage stops are blocked parts live_<stratum>, not the tier. Before any session the harness asks the host as the reader plx.find on each sampled root: an unresolved root gets no session (projection tier roots_unresolved, never an agent failure) and fewer resolved roots than 20 is a blocked part roots_unresolved (missing_bindings); the resolved items are also answered by the deterministic path (no model, same host and reader). Then the 13 exposed F7-F9 real cases on an empty fixture mirror and the pinned 10-item FIXTURE_SAMPLE of evals/dev on the fixture world (stdio case host --fixture, run pins). Reports per part correct / wrong / blocked / justified abstention with coverage beside accuracy, by family, confident_unsupported, originals_not_held, refused tool calls, action calls and citations the harness could not re-read as the reader (unreadable_citations by scheme), eval.tiers keeping access / capture (the host ledger) / projection / deterministic / agent apart, the live sample's strata, and the deterministic baseline's outcomes on the fixture sample beside it. Counts, rates and enums only; transcripts stay in {tmp}.
notes: live-unverified until a passing live-check result; keyless tests drive it with an injected agent transport (evals/tests/test_runner.py RealAgentEvalTests: scripted MCP tool calls through the real tool gate and stdio case host, every outcome class, the k=1 session cap; tests/test_eval_real_agent.py: the live sampler on the fixture world with the Portal down picks only BC-rooted items and blocks the Portal strata, the live host is operating.host mcp with a ticket for the named reader and never --fixture or --principal, without an identity the live part is blocked before any read, and roots the reader cannot resolve get no session and are counted in the projection tier, never the agent's); no real-agent number exists until this check runs. requires_env CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN only (without it the check is skipped). The reader identity, session secret, host state and BC/Graph/Portal names are optional_env so the fixture parts keep measuring while they are missing: until the operator names a real employee reader the live part reads as the eval principal (labelled, never the A6 permission proof), with the fixture parts recorded beside it; with the reader configured a Portal outage blocks only the live Portal strata. No binary, or sessions that all fail without an answer (e.g. no login), is blocked (host_misconfiguration), never a pass. Budget: at most 47 sessions (one per item, k=1, one phrasing), 25 turns and 300 s each, all started inside 2400 s, after the reader check (60 s), the oracle's live reads (900 s), the root probe (300 s) and the deterministic path (600 s): 4260 s, 4560 s with one 300 s session overrun, 240 s under the 4800 s check timeout. Sizing (2026-10-21): measured whole runs in the published results were 617-1019 s for the 23 fixture sessions with the live part blocked before any read (27-44 s per session); 47 sessions at the measured worst are about 2070 s, so 2400 s covers them, and the live phases keep their own ceilings because the live part has never run (a forecast, re-size from the first live run); a session the budget refuses is blocked and the run incomplete (exit 3). Exit 3 also when fewer than 8 runs were scored (non-blocked), the live oracle sampled fewer than 20 items, or read-gap runs exceed 10% of every run (eval.fail_reasons blocked_tripwire, evals.score.fail_reasons: the dev baseline's rule); fewer than 20 roots the reader resolves is blocked (roots_unresolved), never a pass. Citation re-reads: the harness re-reads every cited handle as the reader through its own session of the persistent host (evals.harness_reads, a host-code read no agent catalog lists): api:// and original:// as the case runtime's plx.source_citation, bc://, graph-mail:// and sharepoint:// from the host's captures once the reader's own plx.read resolves them (withheld, changed or uncaptured is unreadable, fail closed). Read gap: a stated answer failing only on a bc:// citation the harness still cannot re-read, for bc:// handles the host served the agent in that run and naming a record of the item's chain, is scored blocked (citation_read_gap, counted per part and in eval.tiers.access), never wrong, while a wrong value, an uncited value or an unreadable api:// citation stays wrong; unreadable_citations.bc counts the handles. One reader per run: eval.tiers.access is scope single_reader with its reader count; a reader the host's resolver refuses as an employee (inactive, unverified, not in the Portal snapshot, refused by Entra) is blocked reader_refused before any source read (exit 0), while any other identity refusal (invalid, expired or replayed ticket, tenant or state mismatch) is a harness or host fault and errors (exit 1), and the reader's root probe stops at --root-probe-seconds (300 s; roots left unasked block the part root_probe_incomplete, projection_timeout; a host that ends the session mid-probe blocks it live_host_session_ended, host_misconfiguration). The baseline beside the fixture sample is evals/baseline/dev-fixture.json (deterministic path with plx.investigate plans). Daily at most: it spends the operator's Claude Code plan. The Claude Code login is CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN or its alias PLX_CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (requires_env_any; operating.agent_environment gives the agent session the alias's value as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN when the canonical name is absent or empty, for an environment whose Claude Code session hides its own token from tool subprocesses). B1: the check passes only when eval.total meets accuracy >= 0.8, coverage >= 0.8 and confident_unsupported_rate <= 0.02. A blocked part (a refused host config or reader, a Portal outage) does not excuse the parts that ran: expect_blocked holds eval.total, the parts that ran, to the same bar, so a blocked run whose fixture parts miss it fails. Only a run no agent session answered (agent_unmeasured binary_not_found or every_session_failed, blocked_when) is blocked whole.
